body:
CANONICAL: restart rules, review cadence and a temporary model workaround for Engram (Engram::Fable, 2026-10-03; split from rules-authority-and-landing for size). The controlling text is AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (Authority and Git, Review Cadence) and .claude/commands/review-changes.md. Read the current text when acting. This note records Greg's words and agreed readings, and carries no higher authority than his current word.

RESTARTS (Greg, 2026-10-02 in Advisor session-6219: "Wolę aby agenci zdecydowali na moment restaru Termal. Wtedy kiedy potrzebuja poprawek. To nie jest problem, nie chce przerywać pracy." and "Chwila. Termal muszę zrestartować ja. Engram mogą sami. Wiec do restaru termala oczekuje od nich potwierdzenia kiedy potrzebują to zrobic."). TermAl: Greg performs every TermAl restart; its MOMENT is the agents'. The Engram and TermAl coordinators agree a moment when running work can resume: no full gate mid-run, no reviewer children alive, no landing or install in progress, no recognised test turn mid-run, no evaluation delegation running, every coordinator told. The TermAl coordinator then sends Greg "restart now" through Engram::Advisor, with the build hash and reason. No agent stops or starts the TermAl host. Agents keep working while a restart is pending: no held window, no pausing; work a restart cuts is recovered or rerun. Engram: agents may restart Engram's own processes themselves, only by a supported route. There is no restart command: let a TermAl control sidecar go 5 minutes without control requests (TermAl reaps it and starts the installed build on the next request; the reap is per session), or start a new CLI process. An `engram mcp` server refreshes only when its host session is recreated, which for TermAl sessions means Greg's TermAl restart. NEVER kill any engram.exe process, least of all a live `engram mcp` server: Claude Code does not reconnect a killed stdio MCP server. A new control connection expires issued-but-unbegun grants; begun turns stay open. These rules are in the checked-in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (Authority and Git) since commit 7dd5195 (2026-10-03, item w-06009c591bbb): the standing approval still grants no restart, deploy or global-configuration authority, and only Greg's quoted words grant the TermAl-moment and Engram-route exceptions. Read that text when acting. Deploy and global configuration stay Greg's and need his explicit word.

REVIEW CADENCE (Greg, 2026-09-26, committed 7424da9; adopted coordination rules of 2026-09-13 revision 1 in docs/agent-pair-workflow.md). One parent owns each review input: it runs the gates, freezes, obtains exactly the Codex and Claude pair read-only, consolidates and records. The gate and both reviews run in parallel on one frozen input, and a failed gate discards those reviews. Fix rounds keep both reviewers. Before coding an item: a design review with Engram::Fable and a read-only Codex explorer. During a gate or review, only non-mutating work on the next item. Repeat verification only for a changed input or a concrete failure, recovering existing results first. Report outcomes, blockers and decisions, not ACK chains. TermAl owns the tests of its host safeguards (denied writes, interpreter restrictions); they block an Engram review only with a concrete connection to the review's access or integrity. Kimi's optional third review stays PAUSED (Greg's word relayed to Engram::Opus as mailbox #587) until Greg lifts it; when it lifts, AGENTS.md's paragraph on the optional third review applies (never counted, never blocking, none on a finished round, a justified Medium or higher fixed and reviewed again by the pair). Kimi's stand-in for an unavailable Codex is a separate rule and not paused.

CLAUDE MODEL AVAILABILITY (since 2026-10-02 about 23:25Z): a weekly usage limit refused some Claude sessions and default-model (opus[1m]) reviewer spawns; availability varies by model and time. Pass the model explicitly on every Claude reviewer or evaluator spawn ("opus[1m]", "claude-fable-5-1" or "sonnet"), try another if one is refused, and record each refusal on the item. The pair rule names vendors, not models. Engram::Opus was back at about 02:12Z on 2026-10-03 and is the default coder again.

REPORTING THE TERMAL RESTART (Engram::Advisor corrections #910 and #914, 2026-10-03). Engram::Fable twice named a superseded TermAl build (120e15d5, then 98ff008) in summaries for Greg. Termal::Fable2 supersedes the installed TermAl build often, and his later notices are information only: they are not a fresh "restart now". In Greg-facing summaries, don't name a TermAl build hash from memory. Either quote Fable2's latest notice with its time, or write "the TermAl restart request (reasons w-837 and w-32df) stands; the build is per Termal::Fable2's latest install notice". Keep "restart now" (an ask) separate from an install notice (information).

UPDATE 2026-10-15, commit d10f724: the review-pair stand-in now covers an unavailable Codex OR Claude reviewer, with at most one Kimi stand-in per round and never for both (see rules-throughput). The sentence above, "Kimi's stand-in for an unavailable Codex is a separate rule", now reads "for an unavailable Codex or Claude". Keep passing the Claude model explicitly and record each refusal: a recorded Claude refusal is now what admits the Kimi stand-in.
